bluf: Instrument is Stagwell's Portland and New York brand, product and marketing agency (350+ people), selling design and technology as one system to enterprise technology, wearables and apparel brands, with Web & Product as its only core line. Its dated moves are a Chief Creative Officer returning in August 2026 and a Fast Company finalist nod in September 2026; the record lists no pricing and no jobs. Horus reads it Neutral at 0.9; Monsoon reads Onshore wind at 57.1. What a rival should know: 18 of 20 clients on record are names without described work, and 10 of them, Google, Microsoft and Nike among them, sit on other tracked books.
doing:
The positioning line, "Technology-led brand, product and marketing agency where design meets technology, building brands, products, websites and campaigns that work as one system," decodes to a design and engineering shop that sells the brand, the product and the site as a single build. The headline claim, "twenty-plus years building brands and products for partners such as Google, Spotify, EA, ServiceNow, Uber and Oura," is quoted as a claim.

The sold mix has one lead and core line, Web & Product, scored 3: the product practice and website design and development, with the Nike SNKRS web app, the Nike design system and the Oura and Eventbrite products as the evidence note. AI Automation / Agents, AI Search / GEO, B2B & ABM, Content & Digital PR, Creator & Influencer and Paid Social each score 1; SEO, Paid Search, Programmatic & CTV, Retail Media, Data & Measurement, Email & CRM, CRO and Local score 0. The services list runs from Brand Strategy & Architecture through Agentic Branding, Website Design & Development, Social & Paid Marketing, Content Production Systems, Product Strategy and AI Strategy & Execution. Proprietary lines: Build Week, a pro bono sprint for startups and small businesses, and Playspace. No partner is listed.

Its AI posture is agentic branding (AI ready brand systems), AI brand tooling, AI strategy inside product work and automated content production systems; no audited AI visibility product shows (P1 partial).

Moves in date order: August 2026, Jack De Caluwé returned as Chief Creative Officer, per Little Black Book; September 2026, Playspace named a Fast Company Innovation by Design 2026 finalist. The homepage recognition row cites Webbys, Awwwards, an ADC 2026 merit and Shorty Awards 2026 wins. The record lists no news, job posting or pricing model. Conspicuously absent for a product and web agency: any search, CRO or measurement line above 0, and any described outcome for the work it shows.
clients:
The ICP is enterprise; the verticals on record are technology and SaaS, consumer electronics and wearables, sportswear and apparel, gaming, travel and health; the home market is the US, with Portland and New York listed.

The record names 20 clients, but only 2 carry an observed need: ServiceNow came for brand and creative, the signal being the case slug rebrand (N3), and Sonos for brand, the slug brand (N3). The other 18 are coded N0, engagement named only, and their needs are inferred from the sold mix, web build and platform and brand: Nike (the snkrs case, a web app per the capability note), Google (google holiday 100), Electronic Arts, Oura (the smart ring case), Uber for Business, Microsoft, Levi's, Procore, Notion, Eventbrite, Marriott Bonvoy, PagerDuty, X (technology invention company), PATH, Splice and Salesforce (the salesforce plus slug), with Spotify and Netflix as logos only.

The shared count is 10: Google sits on the huge, r-ga, dept, media-monks, akqa and brave-bison books; Microsoft on code-and-theory, coalition-technologies, aimclear and billion-dollar-boy; Netflix on media-monks, jellyfish, labelium and akqa; Nike on pmg and akqa; Levi's on r-ga and np-digital; Marriott Bonvoy on razorfish and code-and-theory; Oura, Sonos, Spotify and Salesforce on columbia-road, iprospect, adapt-worldwide and webranking.

What the base needs next, tied to the edition: KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation) is the read's best placement, on AI Search / GEO and content scored only 1, so these product brands will likely ask their web builder for the machine readable layer answer engines consume, which the record marks absent (P2). KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out) is its largest headwind, net 0.675 against, so the same buyers likely press its content and paid social hours toward output pricing the record cannot answer (moderate confidence).
house: Say and do: the Radar ran no say/do test on this house and flagged no gap. The Transparency Center shows 9 Google ads, 7 in the last 30 days, 7 text, 1 image and 1 video, last shown 2026-09-27, under the advertiser names Instrument and 28 CR RTM COMPANY LIMITED; no sample is recorded. LinkedIn ads are not found: 5,250 ads match the name query, the one dynamic card belonged to an instrumentation company, and the record shows 0 company page ads. No llms.txt is published and no AI crawlers are listed as blocked. The tag stack is gtm alone on Nuxt, Storyblok and Craft CMS; no social pixels, test tools or ABM stack show, which is thin for a house that sells social and paid marketing.

openings:
The strongest opening is the shopping book: 10 of 20 clients on record already sit on other tracked agencies' books, Google on six of them, and 18 of 20 are names without described work, so a rival with a described product or web build for a technology or wearables buyer is likely to get a hearing at Nike, Oura, Microsoft or Levi's (moderate confidence). The falsifier: a refreshed instrument.com work section describing outcomes for those accounts at the next compile.

Second, the unclaimed machine readable layer: it builds websites and products as its only core line yet shows no feed, schema or entity work (P2 absent) and no audited AI visibility product (P1 partial), so a rival that ships the site and the answer engine layer together very likely wins that comparison.

Third, the idle house: 145 sitemap URLs with 0 updated in 365 days, no llms.txt, 0 LinkedIn ads and 9 Google ads, so a rival can very likely out publish it on the agentic branding topic it sells. With no public pricing model (P5 unknown) an outcome priced offer meets no public answer; displacement reads 49.6, so a pure rate attack is unlikely to move enterprise buyers.
watch: I8, holdco Q3 organic growth, headcount and pricing model disclosures, October 2026: output or outcome pricing announced at a top five holdco, with Stagwell as its owner, would land on its P5 silence and deepen the KJ6 headwind.

I2, Alphabet Q3 2026 search growth and AI Mode ad disclosures, late October 2026: growth below 10% flags cannibalization, while above 15% with AI Mode ads live confirms S1 and the KJ1 tailwind it is best placed for.
I10, Reddit US daily users against search referral volatility, late October 2026: US DAUq growth at or below 5% alongside AI Mode growth confirms the UGC starvation risk under KJ1.

I6, platform AI labeling enforcement after the EU Article 50(2) deadline, 2 December 2026: new reach penalties for unlabeled AI personas or engagement would strengthen KJ8, its second tailwind, on creator and content work.

The August 2026 return of Jack De Caluwé as Chief Creative Officer is the dated move to follow up, and the next Radar compile (the dossier is only as fresh as 2026-09-28) should show whether the 90 day sitemap count moves off 0 and whether a LinkedIn ad appears.
